The file uses no reference-link definitions, so none were expected or broken. Date is today. PASS.
- Overclaim sweep: no feature named that is not in the branch; no false "all"/"every" statement found. The four-class and 13-code universals were recounted above and hold.

FAILING CLAIM — the `--debug` bullet under Fixed:

  "`mix spec.check --debug` raised `ArgumentError` (`BadBooleanError`) on
   executed `tagged_tests` (and `command`) verification entries because
   command-result maps were used as boolean predicates. Predicates now use
   `is_map(command_result)` on both the findings and checks debug paths"

1. (hard falsehood) `BadBooleanError` is not an `ArgumentError`. Verified empirically on this project's Elixir: `true and %{a: 1} and true` raises a `BadBooleanError` struct with message `expected a boolean on left-side of "and", got: %{a: 1}`, and `is_struct(e, ArgumentError)` is `false`. Nothing rewraps it — there is no `rescue` anywhere in `add_verification_debug_checks` (verifier.ex:1177-~1400), and lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex has no rescue at all, only `Mix.raise` calls. A user grepping logs for `ArgumentError` or writing `assert_raise ArgumentError` is misled by this line.
2. (overclaim) `command`-kind entries never raised. In the pre-fix code (git show fb59b54a) `command_result` was the rightmost `and` operand at verifier.ex:380, :383 and :1258, so it was only truthiness-tested as the `cond` clause value — no BadBooleanError possible. The single crash site was the :1324 clause, where `... and command_result and Map.has_key?(command_result, :attribution)` put the map on the left of `and`. Ticket q0q.1 says the same thing: "verifier.ex:1327 — replace the cond operand chain", with the other four normalizations called "behavior-identical".
3. (mischaracterization) The findings path is not a debug path. `add_verification_command_runtime_findings` (verifier.ex:368) is reached only via `add_verification_findings` (verifier.ex:153) inside `verify_subject`, which runs unconditionally; `debug?` gates only verifier.ex:79 and :116 (whether the `"checks"` key is attached). Ticket q0q.1's Out-of-Scope section names it "the non-debug finding path" explicitly. As written the entry tells a reader the normal findings path was crashing, which it was not.

I acknowledge (2) and (3) each admit a charitable parse — "(and `command`)" could mean "and `command` was also normalized", and "the findings and checks debug paths" could bracket as "[findings] and [checks debug]". (1) admits no such reading. I am failing on (1) and asking that (2) and (3) be disambiguated in the same edit rather than left to the reader.

Suggested replacement (single bullet, no scope change):

  - `mix spec.check --debug` raised `BadBooleanError` on executed
    `tagged_tests` verification entries whose merged command result was a map:
    the map sat on the left of a strict-boolean `and` in the debug-checks
    clause. That clause now guards with `is_map(command_result)`, and the
    equivalent truthy-map operands on the `command` and `tagged_tests` findings
    path were normalized to `is_map/1` alongside it (behavior-identical)
    (specled_-q0q.1)

Targeted verification:
- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` — clean, no output.
- `mix format --check-formatted` — exit 0.
- `mix spec.check --no-run-commands --base 87531f84` — FAILS with 1 error: `[ERROR] branch_guard_missing_subject_update CHANGELOG.md :: Changed file CHANGELOG.md impacts subject specs that were not updated: specled.package`. This is an artifact of the intra-epic base, NOT a defect in this commit: the required `.spec/specs/package.spec.md` co-change landed in b76b48a4 (q0q.4), which is one commit *before* 87531f84 and therefore invisible at that base.
- `mix spec.check --no-run-commands --base af18bad8` (main — the real PR base) — `spec.check result=pass`, 4 findings, all `:info`. This is the ruling run. The release metadata produces no error-level branch findings against main.
- Tests: none expected for release metadata — none added. Correct.
- Full-suite verification: not run by verifier (by design).

Verdict: FAIL

Gaps:
1. CHANGELOG.md, 0.13.0 "Fixed" section, `--debug` bullet: names the exception as `ArgumentError (BadBooleanError)`. `BadBooleanError` is a distinct exception struct and is not an `ArgumentError`; no rescue rewraps it. Fix: name `BadBooleanError` alone.
2. Same bullet: "(and `command`)" attributes the raise to `command`-kind entries, which never raised (pre-fix, `command_result` was the rightmost `and` operand at verifier.ex:380/:383/:1258). Fix: separate "what crashed" from "what was normalized alongside".
3. Same bullet: calls the findings path a "debug path". It is unconditional (verifier.ex:153 via `verify_subject`); `debug?` gates only verifier.ex:79/:116. Fix: as in the suggested replacement above.

All three are in one bullet and the fix is confined to CHANGELOG.md — no code, spec, or VERSION change is implied, so the corrected commit stays inside this ticket's Allowed globs.

Notes (advisory only, not gating):
- The worktree carries an untracked, non-gitignored `.grok/sandbox.toml` (agent session artifact). It is not in the commit so it is not a scope violation, but it inflated `changed_files` in my base-87531f84 spec.check run and will show up in `git status` for whoever cuts the PR. Worth removing or gitignoring before the PR.
- The q0q.5 bullet's "hand-maintained catalogs in the review HTML and severity-integration tests" reads most naturally as placing a self-asserting catalog in lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex. The equality assertions actually live in html_test.exs and severity_integration_test.exs; html.ex's governance `codes:` list is pinned only transitively, because html_test iterates its own emitter-equal catalog and asserts each code flips the row. The intended parse ("the review-HTML tests and the severity-integration tests") is available and accurate, so I did not fail it — but "in the review HTML *tests*" would remove the ambiguity if the bullet is being edited anyway.
